decisions.statement: A question reached by a different key is the same index.
A question no index answers makes a new index.
An index is derived.
An index page names the answers filed.
The code beside the index page files that and nothing else.
An index states its test.
Every index is written as a change lands.
No index is ever built anew; every write lays a delta over what is there.
An index states whether git holds the answers that index files.
The index is written under `.index` at the root of the checkout reading it.
Git holds the answers of an index whose own page says so, and no others.
A change carries those answers among its own file changes.
The index can be written again from the pages alone.
An index file is named for the value that index file answers.
An index file's name closes with `.jsonl`.
The file carries one answer to a line.
An index's answers are filed under a folder named for that index.
That folder is read from the index's own page.
A question no answer covers is answered here rather than by the caller asking.
A caller outside spells no directory the index files under.
A value no page carries has no file.
A question the index answers is read from the index rather than from the pages.
A directory is divided into no buckets.
The index is written by akasha's own code and by nothing else.
A long-running process akasha spawns writes here as a command does.
A path in the index is relative to the repository root.
The index has every page.
The index has the pages rather than every file git tracks.
No page's entry is older than the files its properties have.
Nothing in the index differs from the pages.
A fixture files a page into every index a reader reads that page from.
A fixture takes a page out of every index answering for that page.
A question and its answer cross this boundary.
The index crosses this boundary as a change leaves the index.
Nothing more crosses this boundary.
A question answered once over one reading is held rather than worked out again.
No reader asks whether an index is whole before reading that index.
An index is read while a refresh writes that index.
A file is put in place whole, so a reader reads it as it was or as the refresh left it.
A refresh takes away every path under the index that the pages do not imply.
A folder under the index that no index page names goes with the next refresh.
A pattern written under the index or under a cache is Alan's to approve before it is written.

definition: one question the pages can be asked, answered by reading one file
